L.title: Gate release does not cover failures in the observation query
L.scenario: Unexpected-table and exhausted-poll paths release the gate, but a database/query exception, cancellation, or scalar_one_or_none raising for multiple matching waiters propagates before either release. The paused writer can remain waiting with locks held until outer test teardown cancels it, obscuring the original failure or delaying cleanup. A probe executing the exact pinned blocked_by/assert_blocked functions with an injected observation-query error confirmed that the exception propagates while gate.release remains unset.
L.fix: Release the gate in a finally block around observation/assertion and ensure spawned writer tasks are awaited or cancelled on failure. Prefer fetching PID/query pairs and matching the intended contender when multiple waiters are possible.

L.title: The cross-subject contention claim needs a disjoint-master qualification
L.scenario: The added paragraph says across subjects contention exists only on profile and grant heads. Distinct assessed subjects can share a root or dependency artifact key, and lock_subject_masters locks all those authority rows. They therefore can also contend on master rows. The intended argument about residual contention applies to disjoint master-row sets. This does not reveal a runtime cycle because the master rows themselves are sorted.
L.fix: Replace 'across subjects' with 'across subjects with disjoint master-row sets' and keep the later-head/fixture limits explicit.

conditions.status: CARRIED; not an additional B3 blocker under the inspected custodian/reader reuse
conditions.judgment: Pinned admit calls the current locked checkpointed grant reader in the owning selection transaction, maps an unavailable/inactive/revoked grant to DispositionUnauthorizedError, and compares current sequence/event digest with the stored lease. The reader rejects non-ISSUE/inactive grants and checkpoint/head disagreement. A fresh function-level probe of the exact pinned admit method admitted an unchanged grant and refused changed sequence, changed digest and revoked/unavailable reader results. This supports carrying the missing integration fixture rather than leaving a demonstrated source defect open.
conditions.requirement: Persist a real grant transition after lease issuance and assert no selection/head advancement before B5 interactive selection route activation or release acceptance. The mocked probe does not prove signed-ledger/checkpoint transitions or real DB locking.

conditions.status: CARRIED; not an additional B3 blocker
conditions.judgment: authorize_selection's transaction appends only a lease. It never writes a selection or packaging head. select uses one session.begin transaction for selection append and head CAS, so a crash before select leaves an inert lease, and an uncommitted partial append/head update is a database transaction recovery concern. The accepted A6 shape and source provide a bounded argument; no B3 crash execution is claimed.
conditions.requirement: Add B3-specific crash-after-lease and failure-between-selection/head-write recovery tests before integrated route/recovery acceptance. Verify unchanged existing head and retry behavior; do not label the current 37 cases as crash coverage.

Use the actual grant/master/profile waits as the B3 evidence boundary. Publication tests remain repository-level; later head modes and multi-principal/disjoint-master schedules are source-construction arguments. Do not advertise them as observed PG interleavings. Keep N1/N2 as Low follow-ups and preserve a distinct-principal regression as a useful hardening task.

Design section 4 still literally says 'no sleeps' while waiter observation polls with sleep(0.05). Events determine ordering, so this is bounded observation polling rather than a sleep used to guess writer order; clarify that distinction in the spec or replace the polling. The new expiry case sleeps 1.2 seconds after a one-second preview, and the cap test derives a 120-second deadline from host time. Prefer DB-time seams for deterministic, clock-skew-independent expiry regressions. No test flakiness was reproduced here.
